result:
`GET /health` now runs a real database probe on every request instead of returning a static `200 {"status":"ok"}`.

**`routes/web.ts`** — wires `@guren/core`'s `HealthManager` + `DatabaseCheck` (both re-exported from `@guren/server`) with `critical: true`, and a small `DatabaseConnection` adapter whose `query()` calls `getDatabase()` (from `config/database.ts`) and runs `SELECT 1` via the Drizzle instance's `.run()` on every check — no caching. The `/health` handler runs `healthManager.check()` per request and returns `{ status, checks: { database: { status, message, duration } } }` with HTTP `200` when healthy and `503` when the DB check comes back `unhealthy` (a thrown/timed-out query), so a broken deploy actually gets drained instead of staying `200`.

**`tests/health.test.ts`** (new) — an integration test hitting the real app confirms the happy path (`200`, `status: "healthy"`, `checks.database.status: "healthy"`), plus three unit-level tests against the same `HealthManager`/`DatabaseCheck` primitives verifying that a failing critical DB check produces an `unhealthy` report (and thus the route's `503` mapping), since forcing the shared SQLite connection to fail without corrupting later tests isn't practical.

`bun run typecheck`, `bun test` (6 pass, 0 fail), and `bunx guren check` (0 failures, pre-existing warnings only) all pass.
